subject: mata mata turtle
title: This Turtle Looks Like a Rotting Leaf, Then Vacuums Fish in 20 Milliseconds

scenes.text: That isn't a dead leaf on the riverbed. It's waiting for a fish.
The mata mata, an Amazon turtle with a shell up to 45 centimeters, built like bark and driftwood, lies almost motionless.
It rarely swims. It walks the bottom and lets the camouflage work.
Then a fish drifts past. Its mouth gapes to 80 degrees and its throat balloons, so fast that water and fish rush in. Twenty milliseconds.
Its jaws are weak, so it never bites. It holds the fish in its throat, slowly pushes the water out, and swallows.
A predator that eats without ever biting. The leaf has a stomach.

description:
The mata mata turtle of South America hunts by suction, not by biting.
Chelus fimbriata lives in slow blackwater rivers, flooded forests and lakes of the Amazon and Orinoco basins, with a knobbly, leaf-shaped shell up to about 45 cm long that looks like bark or driftwood. It rarely swims and lies nearly motionless on the bottom. When a fish comes close, it lunges, opens its jaws to about 80 degrees and expands its throat so quickly that water and prey are sucked in: photo sequences show the prey engulfed within about 20 milliseconds, with the throat fully extended by 44 milliseconds. Its jaws are weak, so it holds the fish in its throat, slowly expels the water and swallows.
What other animal is a master of disguise?
first_comment: It never bites: the fish is sucked in within 20 milliseconds. Which camouflaged animal has fooled you?
